ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
The festive square is adorned with hydrogen balloons bearing celebratory slogans. As shown in the figure, a hydrogen balloon with a mass of $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is tethered by a light rope and floats in the air. The light rope attached to the hydrogen balloon makes an angle of $\theta=37^{\circ}$ with the vertical direction. The other end of the rope is tied to a wooden box with a mass of $M=9\mathrm{kg}$. The buoyant force exerted by the air on the hydrogen balloon is constant at $F_{buoyancy}=18\mathrm{N}$, directed vertically upward. The gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$. The wind force and buoyant force acting on the wooden box are negligible.

1. The magnitude of the horizontal wind force and the magnitude of the tension in the rope.
2. The magnitude of the normal force exerted by the ground on the wooden box and the magnitude of the frictional force.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: In the attached diagram, the balloon is located above and to the left of the object on the ground. A rope runs diagonally down-right from the balloon to the ground object/box. Near the ground object there is a dashed vertical reference line, and the rope makes a labeled angle of 37° with this vertical line. Several wind arrows on the right side point horizontally to the left. Reasoning: Use separate equilibrium conditions for the balloon and the wooden box. Given m=1 kg, M=9 kg, F_buoyancy=18 N upward, g=10 m/s^2, sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8. For the balloon, the forces are buoyancy upward, weight mg=10 N downward, wind force leftward, and rope tension T along the rope toward the box, i.e. down-right. Vertical equilibrium gives 18 - 10 - T cos37° = 0, so T cos37° = 8 N, hence T = 8/0.8 = 10 N. Horizontal equilibrium gives wind force = T sin37° = 10 × 0.6 = 6 N. For the wooden box, the rope pulls up-left with components T cos37°=8 N upward and T sin37°=6 N leftward. The weight is Mg=90 N downward, the ground normal force is upward, and friction acts rightward. Vertical equilibrium gives N + 8 - 90 = 0, so N=82 N. Horizontal equilibrium gives friction = 6 N.

method.method_draft: Use a mixed force-triangle plus whole-system equilibrium route. First describe the image: the balloon is pulled by a slanted rope whose direction is 37° away from vertical, and the wind arrows are horizontal to the left; the box is on the ground at the rope’s lower end. From the text, compute the balloon’s upward surplus force excluding tension and wind: F_buoyancy - mg = 18 - 10 = 8 N upward. Since the balloon is in equilibrium, the tension must have an 8 N downward vertical component, so T cos37°=8 and T=10 N. The same force triangle gives the horizontal component T sin37°=6 N, which must balance the horizontal wind force, so wind force is 6 N. For the box quantities, avoid a detailed box-first calculation by considering the combined balloon+box system. Internal rope tension cancels. Vertically, external forces are total weight (m+M)g=100 N downward, buoyancy 18 N upward, and ground normal N upward, so N+18=100 and N=82 N. Horizontally, for the combined system the external horizontal forces are wind left and ground friction right, so friction equals the wind force in magnitude, 6 N.

The festive square is adorned with hydrogen balloons bearing celebratory slogans. As shown in the figure, a hydrogen balloon with a mass of $m=1\mathrm{kg}$ is tethered by a light rope and floats in the air. The light rope attached to the hydrogen balloon makes an angle of $\theta=37^{\circ}$ with the vertical direction. The other end of the rope is tied to a wooden box with a mass of $M=9\mathrm{kg}$. The buoyant force exerted by the air on the hydrogen balloon is constant at $F_{buoyancy}=18\mathrm{N}$, directed vertically upward. The gravitational acceleration is $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$. The wind force and buoyant force acting on the wooden box are negligible.

1. The magnitude of the horizontal wind force and the magnitude of the tension in the rope.
2. The magnitude of the normal force exerted by the ground on the wooden box and the magnitude of the frictional force.

ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description first: In the attached diagram, the balloon is located above and to the left of the object on the ground. A rope runs diagonally down-right from the balloon to the ground object/box. Near the ground object there is a dashed vertical reference line, and the rope makes a labeled angle of 37° with this vertical line. Several wind arrows on the right side point horizontally to the left. Reasoning: Use separate equilibrium conditions for the balloon and the wooden box. Given m=1 kg, M=9 kg, F_buoyancy=18 N upward, g=10 m/s^2, sin37°=0.6, cos37°=0.8. For the balloon, the forces are buoyancy upward, weight mg=10 N downward, wind force leftward, and rope tension T along the rope toward the box, i.e. down-right. Vertical equilibrium gives 18 - 10 - T cos37° = 0, so T cos37° = 8 N, hence T = 8/0.8 = 10 N. Horizontal equilibrium gives wind force = T sin37° = 10 × 0.6 = 6 N. For the wooden box, the rope pulls up-left with components T cos37°=8 N upward and T sin37°=6 N leftward. The weight is Mg=90 N downward, the ground normal force is upward, and friction acts rightward. Vertical equilibrium gives N + 8 - 90 = 0, so N=82 N. Horizontal equilibrium gives friction = 6 N.
